topics.title: Problems
topics.text:
Source: http://artofproblemsolving.com/community/c363915h1342538_practice_test



1. Buckets of water at Water Mart cost a fixed price for each bucket, and a price per gallon of water in the bucket. All buckets cost the same, because they each hold 6 gallons of water. If a half full bucket costs $12 less than a full bucket, what is the typical price per gallon?



2. Three circles are externally tangent to each other. If the radius of the circles are 3, 4, and 5, then find the perimeter of the triangle formed by their centers.



3. A group of 6 distinct patients at a hospital are sorted into healthy and infected groups. If at least one of Al, Betty, and Carl are infected, how many possible outcomes of the sorting are there? Assume the order in which they are sorted does not matter.



4. How many pairs of primes add up to 2017?



5. An isosceles trapezoid has side lengths 1, 1, 1, and 2, in that order. An ant starts at one corner, and must travel to the opposite corner. What is the distance it must travel?



6. There is a function $f(x)$, that satisfies $f(x)-f(x-2)=f(x+1)$. If $f(1)=2$, $f(2)=4$, and $f(3)=3$, then what is $f(2016)$?



7. How many ways can 3 red, 3 green, and 3 blue people be seated in a line such that no two people with the same color sit next to each other?



8. A regular tetrahedron is inscribed in a sphere. Given that the radius of the sphere is 6, find the side length of the tetrahedron.



9. When graphed in the complex plane, the solutions to $x^3-1000=0$ form an equilateral triangle. Find the area of this equilateral triangle.



10. We want to design a new Clash Royale unit, the $sxu$, such that it satisfies certain properties. Of the 576 tiles in a typical arena, when the $sxu$ is in the bottom right corner, it has $a$ tiles that it can hit normally at a time, $b$ that it can only hit when it is enraged, and $c$ that it cannot hit at all. Given that my $sxu$ is in the bottom left corner, what is the maximum possible value of $(a)(bc-1)+(b)(ac-1)+(c)(ab-1)$? Assume the $sxu$ does not take up any space.

topics.title: An Incorrect Proof that sqrt(2) = 1
topics.text:
This post was inspired by this one.



Let us define a real number $x$.



We can define $\sqrt{x^2} = x^1$.



We can also say that $\sqrt{x^2} = x^{2^{\frac{1}{2}}} = x^{\sqrt{2}}$.  Since $x^1=x^{\sqrt{2}}$, $\sqrt{2} = 1$.

topics.title: Math Word Problems
topics.text:
1.) A cattle train left Miami and traveled towards New York. 14 hours later a diesel train left traveling at 45km/h in an effort to catch up to the cattle train. After traveling for 4 hours, the diesel train finally caught up. What was the cattle train's average speed?



2.) A car traveled at 4,400 ft per minute. If the radius of each tire is 1 foot, how many revolutions does one of these tires make in a single minute? (use the approximation 22/7 for pi)



3.) For the first 150 miles of a trip, a car drives at v mph. For the next 200 miles, the car drives at (v+25) mph. The average speed of the whole trip is 35mph. Find the value of v.



4.) A car travels at one speed for 4 hours and then at twice that speed for 6 hours. The average velocity for the 10 hour trip is 40mph. Find the initial speed in mph.



5.) The mean weekly salary of 6 teachers in a school is $1,000. If there are 9 teachers and 11 assistant principals and the mean weekly salary for assistant principals and teachers is $1,275, what is the mean salary of the assistant principals?



6.) Train a, traveling at 200mph leaves the station at 1:00pm. Both stations are directly across from each other and x miles away. If the trains meet at 4:00pm, what is x? (I am not sure about this problem, the problem does not say anything about the other train.)

topics.title: Game Theory Problem
topics.text:
Suppose that in a fantasy battle game, people participate in a tournament occasionally.



The tournament consists of $n$ people, all different levels, from $1$ to $n$.



Each person has $n$ health, and an attack that deals $i$ damage, where $i$ is their level.



The person with the lowest level gets the first attack. When he attacks, he chooses a target, and decreases the target's health by his attack damage. If the target has a nonpositive health, the target is eliminated.



They then go in order, with the person with the highest level going last.



Assume that everyone is a perfect logician, and if they are going to die, they eliminate the person that poses the greatest threat.



The question is, given any $n$, who will be the last left standing?

Is there a formula?



Examples I have evaluatedn=2: Guy 1 attacks Guy 2, Guy 2 attacks Guy 1, 2 wins

n=3: Guy 1 attacks Guy 2, Guy 2 attacks Guy 3, Guy 3 attacks Guy 2, Guy 1 attacks Guy 3, 1 wins

n=4: Guy 1 attacks Guy 2, Guy 2 attacks Guy 1, Guy 3 attacks Guy 4, Guy 4 attacks Guy 3, Guy 1 attacks Guy 2, Guy 2 attacks Guy 4, Guy 1 attacks Guy 2, Guy 2 attacks Guy 1, 2 wins

topics.text:
2 lines of general notesknowing formulas is often significant in math contests

whether u solve a problem could be dependent on whether u know a certain formula


so I'm going to make a formula marathon!

rulespost a formula, property, concept, theorem, algorithm, trick, etc. that is helpful for any contest that is AIME level or below

things that u may want to include;

how to use formula (whats the point of knowing a formula if u don't know how to use it?)

in what types of situations can this formula be helpful? (example: sine/cosine law is helpful if u want to solve a triangle and u either have a scientific calculator or the given angles and sides makes use of the fact that sin, cos, tan, csc, sec, cot of a multiple of 15 degrees can be computed without scientific calculator)

examples of this formula being applied (post a problem or thread and give us detailed solution)

tips and tricks (examples: other forms of the formula or computation shortcuts relating to the formula

other important facts or information about the formula

if someone makes a mistake in a formula, politely correct them


incentive that will encourage u to discuss more formulasu get points for posting a formula

+1 point per new formula

if u find that someone posted a repetitive formula, plz quote both the original post of the formula and also quote the repetitive post, and change the repetitive poster's score so that the repetitive formula was worth +0 points


Leaderboard1. OK_then… 1


this is the format that should be used:

Formula 1: How to compute exact value of sin/cos of 15k degrees without calculator where k is an integerim assuming u all know sin/cos/tan of 0, 30, 45, 60, 90, etc. degrees.

heres a formula:

$$tan(a+b)=\frac{tan(a)+tan(b)}{1-tan(a)*tan(b)}$$heres the variation were gonna use;

$$tan(a-b)=\frac{tan(a)-tan(b)}{1+tan(a)*tan(b)}$$if we set $a=45$ degrees and $b=30$ degrees,

we get $tan(a)=1$ and $tan(b)=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$

substituting this back into $$tan(a-b)=\frac{tan(a)-tan(b)}{1+tan(a)*tan(b)}$$and then simplifying we get $$tan(15)=2-\sqrt{3}$$figuring out tan(75) uses a similar method, except this time we use $$tan(a+b)=\frac{tan(a)+tan(b)}{1-tan(a)*tan(b)}$$with the same substitutions, $tan(a)=1$ and $tan(b)=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$

we get $$tan(75)=2+\sqrt{3}$$using $$tan(15)=2-\sqrt{3}$$we can figure out that $$sin(15)=\frac{\sqrt{2-\sqrt{3}}}{2}$$challengecan any1 simplify $$\frac{\sqrt{2-\sqrt{3}}}{2}$$I'm not sure if it is simplifiable


using $$tan(15)=2-\sqrt{3}$$we can figure out that $$cos(15)=\frac{(2+\sqrt{3})\sqrt{2-\sqrt{3}}}{2}$$another challengecan any1 simplify $$cos(15)=\frac{(2+\sqrt{3})\sqrt{2-\sqrt{3}}}{2}$$I'm not sure if it is simplifiable


now that we know sin, cos, and tan, we can find csc, sec, and cot of 15 and 75 degrees

last challengetry to find csc(15), sec(15), cot(15), csc(75), sec(75), cot(75)
